implementation.mode: Every adapter independently implements parsing, validation, error handling, business rules, and output assembly.
sharedArtifacts: expected exit status and error fragments

acceptance.mode: Each final bundle is executed as a subprocess against the same black-box cases.

authoring.mode: Weighted, evidence-backed review of the committed adapters against a shared 0-4 rubric.
authoring.interpretation: DX and maintainability are workload-specific authoring proxies. Every grade, weight, and evidence note is included in this report; they are not universal framework rankings.
authoring.scoreFormula: For each dimension, sum criterion weight × level / 4, then round to an integer from 0 to 100.

bundle.mode: esbuild ESM bundle, minified, tree-shaken, target node24
bundle.metric: Sum of all runtime .mjs files. oclif uses explicit discovery with shared chunks.
bundle.exclusions: oclif auto-transpilation is disabled and its optional development-only typescript loader is externalized.

source.mode: UTF-8 bytes and non-blank lines in each independent adapter implementation.
source.exclusions: Shared black-box fixtures, tests, build scripts, and report scripts.
source.interpretation: A context metric for implementation footprint, not a code-quality ranking.

runtime.mode: End-to-end wall time of a fresh Node.js process with piped stdout and stderr.
runtime.order: Framework order rotates for every sample to reduce ordering bias.

contract.requirement: Three command groups, four leaf actions, command aliases, and unknown-command handling.
Required positional values plus variadic components and configuration files.
String, integer, boolean, aliased, defaulted, and repeated options across the command groups.
Eight enum domains covering deployment, configuration, platform, and verification choices.
Integer parsing and inclusive ranges for replicas, timeout, canary percentage, and warning limits.
Dependent and mutually exclusive options, including approval/confirm and confirm/dry-run.
Cross-field release policy, image formats, unique slugs, repeated key/value maps, and file extensions.
Non-zero normalized errors plus deterministic text and JSON success output.

dx.label: Type continuity
dx.measurement: How precisely input declarations flow into handlers without assertions, coercion, or duplicated interfaces.

dx.label: Validation authoring
dx.measurement: How much of the tested input policy is expressed beside the input declaration instead of in local control flow.

dx.label: Command composition
dx.measurement: Whether commands can be isolated, nested, registered, and reused without rebuilding parser state by hand.

dx.label: Error authoring
dx.measurement: How much normalized validation and error-boundary behavior the framework provides.

dx.label: Isolated testing
dx.measurement: How directly a command or parser can be exercised with supplied argv and without process-level side effects.

maintainability.label: Rule locality
maintainability.measurement: Whether declarations and their validation relationships remain visible in the same local unit.

maintainability.label: Local glue burden
maintainability.measurement: How much parser-specific validation, normalization, and adapter control flow remains after business logic is excluded.

maintainability.label: Type escape burden
maintainability.measurement: How often parsed values cross assertions, broad records, conversions, or manually duplicated type contracts.

maintainability.label: Command isolation
maintainability.measurement: Whether commands have independent modules or classes with explicit registration boundaries.

maintainability.label: Error boundary
maintainability.measurement: Whether failures converge on one framework-supported boundary instead of per-command catches.

command-composition.evidence: Command classes and handler paths isolate command groups; the benchmark registers the command classes explicitly.

error-authoring.evidence: @Catch and @CommandError provide framework boundaries; the adapter only normalizes benchmark output.

isolated-testing.evidence: Command classes are isolated, while end-to-end parsing still runs through the func runtime.

type-continuity.evidence: Decorator-backed class fields retain their declared TypeScript types through handlers without argument casts.

validation-authoring.evidence: Required, enum, numeric, repeated, dependency, and exclusivity rules are adjacent decorators; release policy remains business code.

command-isolation.evidence: Each command group is represented by a command class with scoped handlers.

error-boundary.evidence: @Catch and @CommandError converge parsing and command failures.

local-glue.evidence: Parser adaptation is carried by decorators; local control flow is primarily workload-specific release policy and output assembly.

rule-locality.evidence: Input shape and reusable validation rules sit on the affected fields; cross-field business policy stays in the handler.

type-escapes.evidence: Handlers consume typed fields and FuncArgs without adapter-level assertions.

command-composition.evidence: The command tree and reusable command factories support separation, with registration performed imperatively.

error-authoring.evidence: exitOverride captures parser failures, while the adapter supplies local catches and normalized output.

isolated-testing.evidence: Command instances can parse supplied argv, although process behavior must be disabled or overridden explicitly.

type-continuity.evidence: The benchmark manually mirrors option declarations with ReleaseOptions, ConfigOptions, and ArtifactOptions interfaces.

validation-authoring.evidence: Required values, choices, parsers, and conflicts are declarative; dependencies and business relationships remain local.

command-isolation.evidence: Subcommands have explicit tree boundaries, but the benchmark keeps registration and handlers in one adapter module.

error-boundary.evidence: Parser errors and action errors require separate local normalization paths.

local-glue.evidence: Argument parsers remove some conversion work, while relationship validation and safe execution wrappers remain local.

rule-locality.evidence: Simple rules are adjacent to options; action-dependent and cross-field rules are implemented in action handlers.

type-escapes.evidence: Manual option interfaces preserve handler types but duplicate the parser declarations.

command-composition.evidence: CommandModule objects isolate builders and handlers and can be registered independently or through a directory hierarchy.

error-authoring.evidence: check and fail integrate with parser errors, while the benchmark still supplies a local catch and normalized output.

isolated-testing.evidence: Command modules and parsers accept supplied argv without requiring process.argv.

type-continuity.evidence: Builder return types now flow into CommandModule handlers without handler casts; an inference helper and external @types package remain necessary.

validation-authoring.evidence: choices, demandOption, conflicts, and implies are declarative; numeric ranges and cross-field policy use three check callbacks.

command-isolation.evidence: Release, config, and artifact are independent CommandModule values with typed builders and handlers.

error-boundary.evidence: fail integrates parser failures, followed by one local catch for benchmark output.

local-glue.evidence: Native relationships remove some glue, but three check callbacks still own numeric and cross-field validation.

rule-locality.evidence: Each check stays with its command builder, but several unrelated rules accumulate inside the callback.

type-escapes.evidence: Typed builder inference removes handler assertions and boundary coercions; one helper connects builder and module generics.

command-composition.evidence: Independent Command classes and explicit discovery provide strong command boundaries with framework registration.

error-authoring.evidence: The Config catch handler centralizes framework failures; the benchmark adds output normalization.

isolated-testing.evidence: Command classes are independently addressable but require the oclif config and discovery harness.

type-continuity.evidence: Args and Flags infer parsed values in command methods; the extracted release helper duplicates a ReleaseFlags interface.

validation-authoring.evidence: Required values, options, integer ranges, repeated values, dependsOn, and exclusive are declarative; business policy remains local.

command-isolation.evidence: Every leaf action is an independent Command class discovered through one registry.

error-boundary.evidence: Config supplies a shared catch handler for command failures.

local-glue.evidence: Flag parsing and relationships need little adapter glue; workload-specific release and artifact policy remains local.

rule-locality.evidence: Most input rules sit in static Args and Flags declarations; business policy sits in command methods or the shared release helper.

type-escapes.evidence: Parsed args and flags remain typed, with one manually mirrored interface at the shared release helper boundary.

command-composition.evidence: Command schemas provide basic grouping, while nested behavior and normalization are assembled locally.

error-authoring.evidence: The adapter owns validation errors, catching, formatting, and exit status.

isolated-testing.evidence: The parser can receive argv, but command behavior remains coupled to local normalization and execution wrappers.

type-continuity.evidence: Handlers receive broad option records and locally narrow or convert parsed values.

validation-authoring.evidence: Command schemas describe option presence, while required, enum, numeric, repeated, and relationship validation is local.

command-isolation.evidence: Command schemas create named sections, but parsing, validation, and handlers share one adapter module.

error-boundary.evidence: A local catch normalizes every parser and handler failure.

local-glue.evidence: Most validation and parsed-value normalization is implemented by adapter helpers and handler control flow.

rule-locality.evidence: Option schemas and their required, enum, range, and relationship rules are split across declarations and handlers.

type-escapes.evidence: Broad records and local conversions form the command-handler boundary.

scale.label: absent
scale.meaning: The tested workflow has no practical support for this criterion.

scale.label: local
scale.meaning: The adapter implements the concern locally with little framework help.

scale.label: mixed
scale.meaning: Framework primitives help, but recurring local glue is still required.

scale.label: supported
scale.meaning: The framework carries the concern with small integration code.

scale.label: direct
scale.meaning: A typed framework mechanism carries the concern without duplicate rules.
